correctness.rationale: The exact covariance formula follows by adjacent categorical triple enumeration, and Cauchy–Schwarz proves the strict positive gap outside uniform distributions. A self-contained independent-block Lyapunov proof yields N(0,sigma²). For every n−1-term Bernoulli proxy, Var ≤ mean(1−mean/(n−1)); subsequence compactness and Lindeberg show that all nontrivial limit candidates are N(a,v), v≤tau². Evaluation at ±u proves a uniform lower bound equal to kappa, and Bin(n−1,q) attains it by the independent CLT. Vanishing proxy variance and unbounded mean offsets are handled separately. The exact checker returned 25 checks, not a substitute for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Six specific searches and several variants were made against mathematical record summaries; the accessible 2017, 2019 and 2014 primary HTML literature was inspected at the level of mathematical objects, metrics, and quantifiers. Existing results address distributional constructions, fixed-composition transition covariance, and non-minimax approximations. No inspected theorem supplies the exact limit of the infimum Kolmogorov distance over all independent Bernoulli proxies with at most one term per transition. The previously established finite binary nonrepresentability is subsumed as context but does not entail a nonzero asymptotic best-approximation constant. Historical abstract-only sources and indexing risk remain.

value.rationale: The natural one-independent-trial-per-adjacent-transition modeling class is common when representing run changes; the result gives the exact nonzero asymptotic best-possible CDF approximation error over all heterogeneously tuned Bernoulli proxies, not merely an elementary finite moment mismatch. The sharp formula exposes a uniform/nonuniform phase boundary and provides an explicit model-design benchmark. It is a complete natural fixed-source asymptotic classification, not an arbitrary finite calculation.
